claims.text: A Service with spec.clusterIP: None is headless: no cluster IP is allocated, kube-proxy does not handle it and the platform does no proxying or load balancing for it.

For a headless Service with a selector, the cluster DNS returns A records for the Service name that point directly at the IP addresses of the Service's ready Pods; the client connects to a Pod address itself.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Services > Headless Services > With selectors; DNS for Services and Pods > A/AAAA records

claims.text: A StatefulSet's spec.serviceName names the headless Service that governs its Pods' network identity; each Pod gets <pod name>.<service>.<namespace>.svc.<cluster domain>; the cluster domain is cluster.local unless otherwise configured, as in staging.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: StatefulSets > Stable Network ID (table of cluster domain, service, pod DNS); headless-dns.txt resolves rabbitmq-0.rabbitmq-headless.donhang.svc.cluster.local

claims.text: A headless Service alone gives no Pod a DNS name built from the Pod's own name (CoreDNS may still serve IP-derived names); the StatefulSet's serviceName gives each Pod a name from its Pod name.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: DNS for Services and Pods > Pod's hostname and subdomain fields; StatefulSets > Stable Network ID

claims.text: Nothing keeps a replaced StatefulSet Pod's old IP address; in the run it gets a new one ('address changed: yes'). Its DNS name, built from the Pod name, stays the same and resolves to the new address.

A Service of type ClusterIP (the default) with no clusterIP field gets a cluster IP allocated; its DNS name resolves to that cluster IP and connections to it are passed on to a ready Pod matching the selector.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Services > Type ClusterIP; k8s.l1.services, k8s.l1.service-and-dns

claims.text: RabbitMQ keeps a node's data in a directory named after the node name: RABBITMQ_MNESIA_DIR defaults to $RABBITMQ_MNESIA_BASE/$RABBITMQ_NODENAME, base /var/lib/rabbitmq/mnesia on Linux (output lists the folder rabbit@rabbitmq-0.rabbitmq-headless...).
claims.source_hint: rabbitmq.com docs: Configuration > Environment Variables (RABBITMQ_MNESIA_DIR, RABBITMQ_MNESIA_BASE); File and Directory Locations; headless-dns.txt

claims.text: RABBITMQ_NODENAME sets the node name, of the form prefix@host (here rabbit@<pod DNS name>); RABBITMQ_USE_LONGNAME=true makes RabbitMQ use fully qualified host names in node names.
claims.source_hint: rabbitmq.com docs: Configuration > Environment Variables (RABBITMQ_NODENAME, RABBITMQ_USE_LONGNAME)

claims.text: In a container env, value $(POD_NAME) expands to the earlier env var POD_NAME, set from fieldRef metadata.name, the Pod's own name.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Define Dependent Environment Variables; Expose Pod Information to Containers Through Environment Variables

claims.text: Members of a replicated database or joined RabbitMQ servers reach one particular member (a PostgreSQL standby connects to its primary by host; RabbitMQ nodes and CLI tools address a node by its node name, which must resolve).
claims.source_hint: rabbitmq.com docs: Clustering > Node Names (Identifiers), Hostname resolution; CLI Tools > Node names; PostgreSQL 17 docs: primary_conninfo

claims.text: Opinion: a client that any Pod can serve should use the normal Service rather than a per-Pod name, when it does not need one particular member.
